correctness.rationale: Bridge-cut subgroup obstruction forbids a once-used edge; minimal 2|E| full-support identity words therefore use every edge twice. For a locally noncrossing double-occurrence word, cancellation of the closest complete pair inside any contiguous factor removes only a transposition commuting with all intervening ones; iterating leaves pairwise distinct forest edges. Their product merges precisely the forest components, proving the fixed-vertex parity lemma. Leaf-edge deletion and this lemma prove the iff statement by induction, with leaf and one-edge boundaries checked. Independent enumerator checked exactly 7,740 complete double-occurrence words on five explicit path/star/branching trees (3 or 4 edges): permutation identity agreed with incident-pair nonalternation on each. This does not replace the all-tree induction.
